my-gateways.alt: My gateways in Open MCP Portal: the gateways the signed-in person can use, each with its URL on portal.example.com, why they have access, and Connect snippets for Claude Code, VS Code, Cursor and curl.
my-gateways.caption: Every gateway has one URL. Interactive clients sign in in the browser; scripts and clients that can't sign in use an API key.

catalog.alt: Catalog: published MCP servers from Example Corp's teams, each with its team, health and counts of approved tools, prompts and resources, and badges for servers that need a sign-in or record call contents.
catalog.caption: The catalog lists only published servers, and only the capabilities whose current definition was approved.

server-sign-in.alt: Team › MCP servers › Add server with Authentication set to OAuth: each person signs in, after Detect sign-in: the authorization server, scopes supported, S256 supported and how the portal registers its client.
server-sign-in.caption: Detect sign-in reads an OAuth-protected server's metadata, such as GitHub's hosted MCP server, and shows what is still needed.

gateway-capabilities.alt: A team gateway's Capabilities tab, Choose capabilities: tools, prompts and resources from the team's own servers and the catalog, searchable by name, title or server, some with a minimum team role.
gateway-capabilities.caption: A gateway exposes only what was selected for it, named server__tool so tools from different servers never clash.

oauth-consent.alt: The consent page: Cursor wants to use Support tools as you, naming the host that vouches for the app, the gateway, and where the browser goes back to, with Allow and Deny.
oauth-consent.caption: Consent is remembered per person, app and gateway. Apps your platform admins trust skip this page; people still sign in.

connect-confirm.alt: Connect your GitHub account: the request (signed in as, the tool that asked, the gateway, the provider, what is connected now) and each scope GitHub will ask for, marked New or Already allowed.
connect-confirm.caption: A tool that needs a person's own account answers with a one-time link to this page. The token stays in the portal; the AI client never sees it.

admin-usage.alt: Admin › Usage: totals for the range, error rate and p50 and p95 latency, calls per day, and a breakdown by gateway, server, capability, team or kind of caller.
admin-usage.caption: Usage is rolled up hourly and kept for ranges of up to 90 days. There is no grouping by person.

call-detail.alt: A call page: the tool called, who called it and with which client, the gateway and server, the outcome, time, size and request ID, and View contents for a call whose contents were recorded.
call-detail.caption: Call metadata is always kept. Arguments and results only where a team turned recording on: redacted, and every view audited.
